name: JILL J. KAROFSKY, C.J.
description: Concurred, argued that the legislature has the power to suspend common law causes of action, and when a cause of action is abrogated, the constitutional right to a jury trial does not attach.

name: Rebecca Grassl Bradley, J.
description: Concurred, argued that Ramirez's constitutional speedy trial right was not violated because the 46-month delay was not presumptively prejudicial enough to warrant dismissal, especially given Ramirez's delay in asserting the right and lack of particularized prejudice.

name: ZIEGLER, J.
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: HAGEDORN, J.
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: ANN WALSH Bradley, C.J.
description: Concurred, but argued that the majority's analytical shortcut and 'bright-line rule' for speedy trial delays are too exacting on defendants and could undermine the speedy trial guarantee, especially given systemic issues like lawyer shortages.

name: JANET C. PROTASIEWICZ, J.
description: Concurred with Ann Walsh Bradley's opinion, arguing that the majority's approach is too exacting and could undermine speedy trial rights.

name: Rebecca Frank Dallet, J.
description: Concurred, but disagreed with the tone and criticism in ¶37 and n.6 of the majority opinion, finding it unnecessarily dismissive and adversarial.

name: Jill J. Karofsky, J.
description: Concurred, but disagreed with the tone and criticism in ¶37 and n.6 of the majority opinion, finding it unnecessarily dismissive and adversarial.

name: REBECCA GRASSL BRADLEY, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the governor breached constitutional boundaries by partially vetoing a non-appropriation bill and that JCF did not improperly withhold funds appropriated to JCF.

name: BRIAN HAGEDORN
description: Concurred, argued that the statute requiring legislative approval for certain civil case settlements violates the Wisconsin Constitution's separation of powers by interfering with core executive functions.

name: ANNETTE KINGSLAND ZIEGLER
description: Dissented, arguing that the court's decision to dismiss the original action follows the party line rather than the law.

name: ANN WALSH BRADLEY
description: Dissented with majority opinion.

name: REBECCA FRANK DALLET
description: Dissented with majority opinion.

name: JILL KAROFSKY
description: Dissented with majority opinion.

name: JANET C. PROTASIEWICZ
description: Dissented with majority opinion.

name: REBECCA GRASSL BRADLEY
description: Concurred, arguing that the original action petition should not have been granted in the first place, as she had previously dissented from granting it.

name: BRIAN HAGEDORN
description: Concurred, arguing that the court should have dismissed or held the petition in abeyance, as the original action was improperly granted and its issues are addressed in a related case.

name: REBECCA FRANK DALLET
description: Concurred, argued that comprehensive legislation enacted over the last 50 years thoroughly covers the subject of abortion and impliedly repealed the 19th-century near-total ban on abortion.

name: JILL J. KAROFSKY
description: Concurred, argued that the decision shields women and children from brutal consequences of the statute, emphasizing the tragic real-world impact of severe abortion restrictions on health and personal dignity.

name: ANNETTE KINGSLAND ZIEGLER
description: Dissented, argued that the majority's decision is an exercise of judicial will that usurps the legislature's role, fails to apply implied repeal correctly, and is driven by personal preference.

name: REBECCA GRASSL BRADLEY
description: Dissented, argued that the majority erases a law it dislikes, making the court more powerful than the legislature, and that the concurrence rewrites history and broadcasts false narratives.

name: BRIAN K. HAGEDORN
description: Dissented, argued that the court effectively deletes a law from the books, engaging in policymaking, and that the legislature clearly intended to preserve the 1849 statute as an enforceable abortion law.

name: KAROFSKY, C.J.
description: Concurred, argued that the challenged statutes facially violate the Wisconsin Constitution's bicameralism and presentment requirements by allowing JCRAR to alter legal rights and duties outside the legislative branch without proper lawmaking procedures.

name: ANN WALSH BRADLEY, J.
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: DALLET, J.
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: PROTASIEWICZ, JJ.
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: HAGEDORN, J.
description: Concurred in part and dissented in part, argued that the court should have decided the case narrowly, finding JCRAR's indefinite objection to the commercial building code rule unconstitutional as applied, but not issuing a broad facial ruling on all statutes.

name: ZIEGLER, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the majority's decision creates a constitutional imbalance by strictly confining legislative power while expanding executive power, overruling decades of precedent without proper constitutional analysis, and inconsistently applying constitutional principles.

name: REBECCA GRASSL BRADLEY, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the majority's decision takes power from elected representatives and gives it to the executive branch, undermining the nondelegation principle and the People's sovereignty by allowing administrative rules to have the force of law without proper legislative process.

name: JILL J. KAROFSKY
description: Concurred, argued that the governor's partial vetoes were constitutional under Article V, Sections 10(1)(b) and (c) as they satisfied the four deletion veto principles and did not fall under the write-in veto principle.

name: ANN WALSH BRADLEY
description: Concurred with the majority opinion.

name: REBECCA FRANK DALLET
description: Concurred, argued that the petitioners' substantive-part analysis for § 10(1)(b) should be rejected because it is incompatible with long-standing case law, and that the court's precedent allows for a partial veto to change the policy of the original bill as long as it results in a complete and workable law.

name: PROTASIEWICZ, JJ.
description: Concurred with the majority opinion.

name: BRIAN HAGEDORN
description: Dissented, argued that the governor's partial vetoes constituted 'unilateral gubernatorial lawmaking' by creating new law not passed by the legislature, thereby exceeding the constitutional power of a veto which is one of negation, not creation.

name: ANNETTE KINGSLAND ZIEGLER, C.J.
description: Dissented with majority opinion.

name: REBECCA GRASSL BRADLEY
description: Dissented with majority opinion.

name: JILL J. KAROFSKY
description: Concurred, argued that Brown lacked standing because he did not suffer a personal injury to a legally recognized interest as a result of WEC's decision.

name: ANN WALSH BRADLEY
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: DALLET
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: PROTASIEWICZ
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: ANNETTE KINGSLAND ZIEGLER
description: Dissented, argued that Brown has standing because he has a legal right to have local election officials comply with the law, and the alleged failure of the Racine County Clerk harmed that right.

name: REBECCA GRASSL BRADLEY
description: Dissented, argued that the majority misinterprets the term "aggrieved" and unlawfully strips Brown of standing, thereby gutting voters' right to access courts in election law matters.

name: BRIAN HAGEDORN
description: Dissented, argued that the majority denies the existence of the legal right conferred to voters to have local election officials comply with election laws.

name: ZIEGLER, C.J.
description: Concurred, argued that the prosecutor's comments describing the State's evidence as "uncontroverted" were not intended to comment on the defendant's silence and therefore did not violate his Fifth Amendment rights.

name: ROGGENSACK, J.
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: REBECCA GRASSL BRADLEY, J.
description: Concurred with majority opinion and Hagedorn's concurrence.

name: HAGEDORN, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the majority opinion correctly applied U.S. Supreme Court precedent and that the original meaning and historical record of the Fifth Amendment support not extending Griffin further to cover the prosecutor's comments.

name: KAROFSKY, J.
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: DALLET, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the prosecutor's repeated characterization of the victim's testimony as "uncontroverted" violated the defendant's Fifth Amendment rights because only the defendant could have controverted that evidence.

name: ANN WALSH BRADLEY, J.
description: Dissented with Dallet's opinion.

name: ANN WALSH BRADLEY, J.
description: Concurred, argued that Wis. Stat. § 6.87(4)(b)1. allows the use of ballot drop boxes and the previous ruling in Teigen was unsound in principle and should be overruled.

name: DALLET, J.
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: KAROFSKY, J.
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: PROTASIEWICZ, J.
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: REBECCA GRASSL BRADLEY, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the majority's decision forsakes the rule of law by overturning Teigen, which correctly held that ballot drop boxes are illegal under Wisconsin statutes, and that the majority is indulging its policy preferences.

name: ZIEGLER, C.J.
description: Dissented with majority opinion.

name: HAGEDORN, J.
description: Dissented with majority opinion.

name: ANN WALSH BRADLEY, J.
description: Concurred, argued that both motivations and activities must be considered to determine if an organization is primarily religious, finding the petitioners' activities secular and the denial of exemption constitutional.

name: DALLET, J.
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: KAROFSKY, J.
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: PROTASIEWICZ, J.
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: REBECCA GRASSL BRADLEY, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the majority misinterprets the statute by focusing on the nature of activities, leading to unconstitutional religious discrimination and government entanglement.

name: ZIEGLER, C.J.
description: Dissented, argued that the majority's statutory interpretation is incorrect and leads to constitutional violations.

name: HAGEDORN, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the statute should be interpreted as in Justice Rebecca Grassl Bradley's dissent and criticized the majority's reliance on the remedial statute canon.

name: REBECCA GRASSL BRADLEY
description: Concurred, arguing that the court should have also addressed the Uniformity Clause claim, as the Transportation Utility Fee (TUF) violates it by not basing taxation on property value.

name: PATIENCE DRAKE ROGGENSACK
description: Concurred, arguing that the court should have also addressed the Uniformity Clause claim, as the Transportation Utility Fee (TUF) violates it by not basing taxation on property value.

name: KAROFSKY, J.
description: Concurred, delivering the majority opinion, holding that legislative districts must be physically contiguous and enjoining the use of current maps, while rejecting respondents' defenses and declining to order special elections.

name: ANN WALSH BRADLEY, J.
description: Concurred, agreeing that legislative districts must be physically contiguous and that current maps violate the constitution.

name: DALLET, J.
description: Concurred, agreeing that legislative districts must be physically contiguous and that current maps violate the constitution.

name: PROTASIEWICZ, J.
description: Concurred, agreeing that legislative districts must be physically contiguous and that current maps violate the constitution.

name: ZIEGLER, C.J.
description: Dissented, arguing that the majority's decision is judicial activism, disregards stare decisis, and improperly reopens settled redistricting issues based on a change in court composition.

name: REBECCA GRASSL BRADLEY, J.
description: Dissented, arguing that the majority's decision is a political power grab, misrepresents legal precedent on contiguity, and improperly overrides the legislative role in redistricting.

name: HAGEDORN, J.
description: Dissented, arguing that the court is engaging in political power redistribution, abandoning prior principles of finality and stare decisis, and that the case should have been dismissed.

name: REBECCA GRASSL BRADLEY, J.
description: Concurred, argued that WEC's authorization of ballot drop boxes was unlawful, that absentee ballots must be personally delivered by the voter or mailed by the elector, and that WEC's guidance documents should be treated as administrative rules requiring proper promulgation.

name: ANNETTE KINGSLAND ZIEGLER, C.J.
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: PATIENCE DRAKE ROGGENSACK, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the elector must personally mail the absentee ballot to the municipal clerk and that agents are not permitted to mail absentee ballots on behalf of a voter.

name: BRIAN HAGEDORN, J.
description: Concurred, argued that unstaffed drop boxes for absentee ballot return are not permitted and that personal delivery requires a person-to-person exchange with the clerk or authorized representative.

name: ANN WALSH BRADLEY, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the majority's decision creates an unnecessary barrier to voting, misinterprets statutes regarding drop boxes and agent delivery, and undermines democratic norms by sowing distrust in elections.

name: REBECCA FRANK DALLET, J.
description: Dissented with majority opinion.

name: JILL J. KAROFSKY, J.
description: Dissented with majority opinion.

name: JANET C. PROTASIEWICZ
description: Did not participate in the decision.

name: REBECCA GRASSL BRADLEY
description: Concurred, argued that the court's new majority has shown a willingness to rebalance political power by overturning previous decisions, and while this motion is rightfully denied, the court's actions damage its independence and integrity by advancing a partisan agenda.

name: ANNETTE KINGSLAND ZIEGLER
description: Concurred with Justice Bradley's opinion.

name: REBECCA FRANK DALLET, J.
description: Concurred, arguing that Shiffra was unsound in principle due to misinterpreting federal precedent, unworkable in practice, and detrimental to coherence in the law due to undermining victim's rights and the therapist-patient relationship.

name: ROGGENSACK, J.
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: HAGEDORN, J.
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: JILL J. KAROFSKY, J.
description: Concurred, arguing that Shiffra was unworkable in practice and detrimental to coherence, forcing sexual assault victims into an untenable dilemma between disclosing private mental health records or being barred from testifying.

name: REBECCA GRASSL BRADLEY, J.
description: Concurred, arguing that Shiffra was objectively wrong in misinterpreting federal due process and the state action doctrine, which alone provides sufficient reason to overrule it, and criticized the majority's use of public policy.

name: ANN WALSH BRADLEY, J.
description: Dissented, arguing that Shiffra provided a workable, decades-old procedure that balanced defendant and victim rights, and that the majority wrongly discounted stare decisis and misapplied its factors, leaving nothing in its place.

name: ZIEGLER, C.J.
description: Dissented with majority opinion.

name: BRIAN HAGEDORN, J.
description: Concurred, argued that Marsy's Law was validly ratified because the ballot question was not fundamentally counterfactual and the amendment had a single general purpose, and that the "every essential" test is not a constitutional requirement.

name: REBECCA GRASSL BRADLEY, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the judicial power does not extend to political questions and that the court correctly refused to entertain them.

name: ANNETTE KINGSLAND ZIEGLER, C.J.
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: PATIENCE DRAKE ROGGENSACK, J.
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: REBECCA FRANK DALLET, J.
description: Concurred, agreed Marsy's Law was validly adopted but argued the majority's originalist approach was too narrow and that a ballot description must accurately summarize significant changes.

name: JILL J. KAROFSKY, J.
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: ANN WALSH BRADLEY, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the ballot question failed to convey "every essential" of the amendment by not mentioning the diminution of criminal defendants' rights, thus misleading voters and undermining democracy.

name: BRIAN HAGEDORN
description: Concurred, argued that the motion for reconsideration did not meet the court's standards and defended his 'text-and-history' approach to nondelegation challenges.

name: REBECCA GRASSL BRADLEY
description: Dissented, argued that the majority's decision allowed unelected bureaucrats to exercise legislative power, thereby creating a 'fourth branch of government' and misinterpreting historical statutes.

name: ANNETTE KINGSLAND ZIEGLER
description: Dissented, concurred with Justice Bradley's dissenting opinion.

name: PATIENCE DRAKE ROGGENSACK
description: Dissented, concurred with Justice Bradley's dissenting opinion.

name: ANNETTE KINGSLAND ZIEGLER, C.J.
description: Concurred, argued that the affidavit satisfied the constitutional oath or affirmation requirement because the officer was impressed with the duty to tell the truth, prioritizing substance over form.

name: ROGGENSACK
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: REBECCA GRASSL BRADLEY
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: BRIAN HAGEDORN, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the Fourth Amendment oath requirement was met as the affiant knowingly made a true statement under circumstances that impressed upon him the obligation to tell the truth, despite some sloppiness.

name: JILL J. KAROFSKY
description: Concurred with majority opinion and Justice Hagedorn's concurrence.

name: ANN WALSH BRADLEY, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the oath or affirmation requirement is a constitutional imperative requiring an actual act of swearing before a judicial officer, which was not fulfilled, rendering the warrant invalid.

name: REBECCA FRANK DALLET
description: Dissented with majority opinion.

name: HAGEDORN, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the circuit court did not erroneously exercise its discretion by requiring disclosure of the parents' identities to opposing attorneys while allowing their names to remain sealed from the public and the district, and that the request for injunctive relief on the underlying policy was moot or not properly before the court.

name: ANN WALSH BRADLEY
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: DALLET
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: KAROFSKY, J.
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: ROGGENSACK, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the majority abdicated its responsibility by not addressing the critical constitutional issue of parental rights to raise their children and by failing to grant a temporary injunction against the school district's gender identity policy, and that the circuit court erred in not permitting full anonymity.

name: ZIEGLER, C.J.
description: Dissented with dissenting opinion.

name: REBECCA GRASSL BRADLEY, J.
description: Dissented with dissenting opinion.

name: ANNETTE KINGSLAND ZIEGLER, C.J.
description: Concurred, argued that Prehn lawfully retains his position as a holdover because his term's expiration did not create a vacancy under Wis.Stat. § 17.03, and he can only be removed for cause.

name: ROGGENSACK, J.
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: REBECCA GRASSL BRADLEY, J.
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: HAGEDORN, J.
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: REBECCA FRANK DALLET, J.
description: Dissented, argued that Prehn's office became vacant upon his term's expiration, and he should not be able to hold office indefinitely or be protected by for-cause removal after his term expired, which threatens separation of powers.

name: ANN WALSH BRADLEY, J.
description: Dissented with Justice Dallet's opinion.

name: KAROFSKY, J.
description: Dissented with Justice Dallet's opinion.

name: REBECCA GRASSL BRADLEY
description: Concurred, argued that local health officers lacked statutory authority to close schools and that the order unconstitutionally infringed upon the fundamental right to free exercise of religion.

name: ZIEGLER, C.J.
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: ROGGENSACK, J.
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: HAGEDORN, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the decision correctly interprets statutes and applies precedent on religious liberty, but disagreed with the majority's assertion that addressing important constitutional questions is mandatory even when a case can be resolved on other grounds.

name: DALLET, J.

name: Patience Drake Roggensack
description: Concurred, argued that VanBeek was not seized when Oetzel initially took her license to his squad car, but was unlawfully seized when Oetzel returned to her vehicle, retained her license, and continued questioning to hold her until the K9 unit arrived without reasonable suspicion.

name: Rebecca Frank Dallet
description: Concurred, argued that VanBeek was unlawfully seized earlier in the encounter, specifically when Oetzel took her driver's license back to the squad car for a records check, as a reasonable person would not feel free to leave at that point.

name: Ann Walsh Bradley
description: Concurred with the majority opinion and joined Justice Dallet's concurring opinion.

name: Jill J. Karofsky
description: Concurred with the majority opinion and joined Justice Dallet's concurring opinion.

name: Annette Kingsland Ziegler
description: Dissented, argued that VanBeek was not seized at any point, as she was free to ask for her driver's license back and end the interaction, making the entire encounter consensual.

name: Rebecca Grassl Bradley
description: Dissented with the majority opinion.

name: Brian K. Hagedorn
description: Dissented with the majority opinion.

name: BRIAN HAGEDORN, J.
description: Concurred, argued that Halverson was not "in custody" for Miranda purposes under the totality of circumstances, and rejected adopting a per se rule for incarcerated individuals under the Wisconsin Constitution.

name: REBECCA GRASSL BRADLEY, J.

name: ANNETTE KINGSLAND ZIEGLER
description: Concurred with Justice Rebecca Grassl Bradley's opinion.

name: REBECCA FRANK DALLET, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the Wisconsin Constitution was intended to provide greater protections for individual liberties than the federal constitution, and that Knapp II correctly upheld these protections against overbearing law enforcement practices.

name: ANN WALSH BRADLEY
description: Concurred with Justice Rebecca Frank Dallet's opinion.

name: JILL J. KAROFSKY
description: Concurred with Justice Rebecca Frank Dallet's opinion.
